step1_figure.circuit_type: Fully-differential two-stage CMOS op-amp with continuous-time common-mode feedback (CMFB)
step1_figure.description: Figure 26.29 shows the complete schematic of the two-stage fully-differential op-amp including Miller compensation capacitors (50 fF), resistive-capacitive output common-mode sensing network (20 kΩ and 10 fF), and a differential-pair CMFB amplifier with current mirror load that controls the center bias branch.

differential_dc_gain.description: Small-signal low-frequency open-loop differential voltage gain loaded by the CMFB sensing resistors

equation.explanation: Differential gain obtained by differentiating the differential output voltage with respect to the differential input voltage around the balance point.
equation.assumptions: Loaded by 20 kΩ CMFB averaging resistors; devices operating in saturation.

sky130_expected.calculation: gm1 = sqrt(2 * un*Cox * (W/L) * Id1) = sqrt(2 * 270u * 10 * 20u) = 328 uS. First-stage output resistance r_o1 ≈ 1/(2 * lambda * Id) = 1/(2 * 0.1 * 20u) = 250 kΩ. First stage gain Av1 ≈ gm1 * r_o1 ≈ 82 V/V. Second stage loaded by R_load = 20 kΩ: gm2 = sqrt(2 * up*Cox * 40 * 40u) = 400 uS; rout2 ≈ (1/(0.1*40u)) || 20k = 250k || 20k ≈ 18.5 kΩ; Av2 ≈ gm2 * rout2 ≈ 7.4 V/V. Overall differential gain A_v ≈ Av1 * Av2 ≈ 600 V/V (≈ 55 dB). In Fig. 26.30, peak gain is ~300 V/V (49.5 dB).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Resistive loading by the 20 kΩ CMFB network reduces the output stage impedance and lowers the open-loop DC gain from ~500 V/V down to ~300 V/V.

output_common_mode_voltage.description: DC common-mode voltage at which vop and vom cross when differential input is zero

equation.explanation: The CMFB loop senses the average output voltage via R1 and R2 and compares it to VCM, steering bias current to force VOCM = VCM.
equation.assumptions: High CMFB loop gain forces VOCM closely to reference VCM (0.5 V).

sky130_expected.calculation: VCM reference is set to 0.50 V. With loop gain A_cmfb ≈ 200, the steady-state tracking error is (VCM - VOCM) ≈ Delta_V / A_cmfb < 5 mV.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The CMFB amplifier stabilizes the output common-mode level precisely at the reference voltage VCM = 500 mV.

output_voltage_swing.description: Linear output voltage swing range for each single-ended output

equation.explanation: Difference between maximum and minimum linear output voltages before saturation/clipping occurs.
equation.assumptions: The uncascoded output stage limits swing due to elevated gate-source voltages when biased at 500 mV.

sky130_expected.calculation: Text on page 884 notes outputs swing from 200 mV to 800 mV (swing = 0.6 V) due to PMOS/NMOS overdrive in the output buffer. On SKY130 (VDD=1.8V, VCM=0.5V), Vmin is bounded by NMOS Vds,sat (~0.2 V) and Vmax is bounded by PMOS Vds,sat below VDD (~1.5 V).
sky130_expected.reasoning: As explained in 'Origin of the Problem' (page 884), the buffer's quiescent currents increase significantly when Vout is forced to VCM, degrading linear swing.

quiescent_current.description: Total DC quiescent supply current drawn from VDD

equation.explanation: Sum of currents in the bias circuit (50 uA nominal) plus 11 branches in the op-amp and CMFB amplifier.
equation.assumptions: Nominal design expects 270 uA, but simulation shows ~500 uA due to excess current in output stage.

sky130_expected.calculation: Nominal: 50 uA (bias) + 11 * 20 uA = 270 uA. However, as noted on page 884, driving the output to 500 mV drops the PMOS gates, increasing output buffer current to ~2x nominal: I_DD ≈ 450 uA to 600 uA.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The book explicitly highlights that this topology draws around 500 uA instead of the expected 270 uA.

cmfb_amplifier_gain.description: Voltage gain of the CMFB differential amplifier with current-mirror load

equation.explanation: Gain from the sensed average output VCMA to the control node VCMFB.
equation.assumptions: PMOS differential input pair with NMOS active current-mirror load operating in saturation.

sky130_expected.calculation: gm_p = sqrt(2 * up*Cox * 20 * 20u) = sqrt(2 * 50u * 20 * 20u) = 200 uS. rout = ro_p || ro_n ≈ 1/(0.1*20u + 0.1*20u) = 250 kΩ. Ideal gain Av ≈ 200 uS * 250 kΩ = 50 V/V. In practical short-channel/loaded conditions, Baker notes gain ≈ 8 V/V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Figure 26.28b simulation explicitly confirms a gain of approximately 8 V/V.

cmfb_forward_gain.description: Gain from the CMFB control voltage VCMFB to the op-amp outputs

equation.explanation: Common-mode transfer gain from VCMFB node to the op-amp output terminals.
equation.assumptions: VCMFB swept around nominal bias (~400 mV).

sky130_expected.calculation: From Baker's simulation (Fig. 26.27, p. 882), forward CMFB gain is approximately 25 V/V (about 10 times less than the differential gain).
sky130_expected.reasoning: The center NMOS tail device modulates the diff-amp output levels, which steer the output buffers.

cmfb_loop_gain.description: Total open-loop gain of the common-mode feedback loop

equation.explanation: Product of the CMFB error amplifier gain and the op-amp forward common-mode gain.
equation.assumptions: Both stages operating around the nominal common-mode equilibrium point.

sky130_expected.reasoning: As stated on page 882: 'This combined with the op-amp's CMFB gain gives an overall CMFB loop gain of 200 (less than the op-amp's differential gain so we can use the same compensation capacitors).'

step3_testbench.description: Complete ngspice testbench for the op-amp in Figure 26.29. Characterizes DC operating point (quiescent current, common-mode output level), DC transfer sweep (differential open-loop gain, single-ended output swing, common-mode crossing point), and AC frequency response.
